summary: 1934 L-4 cab on a 20-foot steel tower above Bass Lake, now a Forest Service radio relay site; sources conflict on the pre-1934 history.

facts.design: 14 by 14 foot L-4 cab with catwalk on a 20 foot H-braced steel tower; base replaced with a Pacific Coast Steel tower after 1935
facts.status_note: No longer used for fire detection; maintained as a radio relay site. No source read gives a current condition report.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1934 as the build year. fire-lookouts.org says the site was a lookout before 1915, a 1915 cabin blew down in winter 1915-16, and 1934 was a reconstruction. The story reports both and follows the register for the build year.

The 2007 visit report on the register page says the tower has fallen over, but it names the Mendocino National Forest, not the Sierra. It appears to describe a different peak. Not used; the register's own description says the tower is a maintained relay site.
Register and fire-lookouts.org both describe a 20-foot tower. A 2005 visitor comment on the register page says nearly 60 feet. Story does not state a height.

notes_for_editor: Brief build year 1934 matches the register but fire-lookouts.org describes earlier use. The register's 2007 visit report names the wrong forest and was not used. No source read gives current visitor access, so access is omitted. A WebSearch surfaced a Wikipedia article on this lookout and a Sierra News Online page on a gated road to repeater vaults; neither was read, so neither is used. No new photos.
